A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DRBench and DRBA. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching material across renumbering and changes in presentation.

before.justification: Sections 5–6 and the appendices report original agent evaluations, planning and backbone comparisons, iteration ablations, and human evaluations.

after.justification: V2 reports expanded agent evaluations and adds human validation of insight judgments, judge-sensitivity results, and paraphrase-robustness experiments.

M1.justification: The five-stage data-generation pipeline and DRBA's planning, adaptive research loop, retrieval, and report-generation procedures are retained. V2 clarifies structured versus narrative reports without establishing a new algorithmic component or an actual change to the agent.

E1.justification: Beyond increasing task counts, Tables 29–34 add substantive scenarios absent from v1's Table 7, including retail knowledge management, healthcare medication-safety knowledge management, and EV asset management using digital twins. The same three industries remain, but their represented research requirements broaden substantially.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same planning variants, backbone models, browser agent, and commercial comparators, including Perplexity, OpenAI Deep Research, and Gemini. Simple and Complex planning are renamed SRP and CRP. The new judge comparison tests evaluation sensitivity rather than adding a competing research agent.

E3.justification: The reported FullBenchmark expands from 15 to 100 tasks and MinEval from five retail tasks to 15 tasks. Backbone comparisons move from MinEval to FullBenchmark. Section 5.6 changes the local-setting description from files in an accessible folder to files passed directly to agents. New human-validation and paraphrase experiments introduce additional evaluation designs.

E4.justification: V2 adds GPT-4o versus Llama-3.1-405B judge sensitivity in Appendix L, paraphrase robustness in Appendix S, and direct human validation of insight judgments in Section 6. Appendix T newly reports near-perfect recall from copying documents without the cutoff. Existing planning, iteration, and source-type analyses remain.

E5.justification: Three-run averaging and standard-error reporting already existed. V2 adds a four-run paraphrase-variance estimate and Cohen's kappa for human–judge agreement. Table 19's uncertainty values change, but the PDFs do not establish an increased repetition count or a changed estimation procedure for that table.

E6.justification: Major performance tables receive replacement scores under expanded settings: Table 2's base-DRBA recall changes from 16.92 to 13.18, which is not a same-setting decline. Table 5's report-quality leader changes from OpenAI Deep Research to DRBA (GPT-5). V2 also adds judge-agreement and paraphrase results and revises Table 19's error bars beyond percentage conversion.

T1.justification: The task and insight definitions, distractor-avoidance formula, and human-preference scoring formula are retained. The latter moves from Appendix Q to R. No new formal assumptions, proofs, theorems, or substantive mathematical derivations appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion expand the claimed benchmark contribution from 15 tasks and 114 groundtruth insights to 100 tasks and 1093 insights. This substantially enlarges the claimed deliverable. The central enterprise-research positioning and conclusions about agents missing important insights remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive limitations concerning novel insights excluded by the cutoff, coarse attribution, restricted task families, and residual judge bias. Sections 5.2–5.6 expand explanations involving contextual binding, missing-knowledge detection, query formulation, and interaction complexity. The new scope discussion explicitly frames the benchmark as document-centric and diagnostic.

D1.justification: The abstract now advertises code and data rather than code alone, and a new reproducibility statement describes release contents and a permissive license. V2 clarifies structured evaluation inputs and supplies additional task metadata. The detailed implementation, hardware, hyperparameters, container setup, and cost information largely remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Choubey et al. (2025), distinguishing its closed-form enterprise fact retrieval from DRBench's research tasks. Cohen (1960) and Gwet (2001) support the added agreement analysis. The broader related-work taxonomy and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order are retained. V2 makes focused explanatory expansions, adds validation appendices and ethics/reproducibility/limitations statements, shortens the conclusion, standardizes terminology, and updates authorship and conference headers. These changes do not amount to a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands task and validation displays through Table 20 and Tables 29–34. Figures 1 and 3 clarify report formats, Figure 4 is redrawn, and v1's source-type Figure 8 becomes v2's Table 22 with retained values. Several tables also receive revised labels, units, and formatting.

improvement.justification: Broader task scenarios and expanded evaluations substantially strengthen v1's limited benchmark coverage. Direct human validation on 264 insights, reporting over 91.3% agreement, plus judge-sensitivity and paraphrase checks strengthen confidence in the central metric. These gains outweigh reporting problems, including duplicate task entries and stale inventory counts. Section 5.6 also retains an inaccurate all-metrics leadership claim: v2 Table 5 gives DRBA higher report quality than OpenAI Deep Research.
